# Arca Go SDK — AI Context

> github.com/arcaresearch/arca-go-sdk — Go SDK for the Arca financial
> infrastructure platform (accounts, payments, perpetuals trading, real-time
> streaming, audit trails). Hand-written port of @arca-network/sdk (TypeScript).

go get github.com/arcaresearch/arca-go-sdk

Import path is `github.com/arcaresearch/arca-go-sdk`; the package name is `arca`.

## Conventions (Go-specific)

- Every method takes a `context.Context` as its first argument.
- Money/amount values are decimal strings ("50", "0.01").
- Coin ids are canonical `{exchange}:{id}` ("hl:0:BTC", "hl:1:TSLA"), case-sensitive.
- Market-data timestamps are Unix epoch ms; all others are RFC3339 UTC strings.
- Errors are typed; use errors.As. Base type: *arca.ArcaError (has Code, Message, ErrorID).
  Typed: *ValidationError, *UnauthorizedError, *ForbiddenError, *NotFoundError, *ConflictError,
  *InternalError, *ExchangeError, *OperationFailedError, *OperationStalledError,
  *StepUpRequiredError, *StepUpCancelledError.
- Order rejections: a venue refusal is a *ConflictError (409) whose Code is NO_LIQUIDITY (empty book —
  retry or use a marketable limit), MARKET_DELISTED (positions settled by the venue),
  MARKET_NOT_TRADABLE (halted or not yet live), MARKET_NOT_USDC_COLLATERAL, VENUE_RATE_LIMITED (the
  account's venue request allowance is spent — on Hyperliquid it is earned by cumulative volume traded,
  not by elapsed time, so waiting does not restore it and each retry spends budget the account has not
  earned), or ORDER_FAILED (refusal
  with no narrower code; the venue's verbatim reason is in Message). None are retryable as-is — change
  the request. A bad-input refusal (tick size, price band, leverage cap, min notional, insufficient
  margin) is a *ValidationError (400) carrying the same verbatim reason. *ExchangeError (502) means the
  request never got a verdict (connection reset, timeout, unparseable response) and IS retryable.
  Branch on Code, not HTTP status.
- Token-provider clients refresh ~30s before expiry, retry once on 401, and retry once on 403
  (FORBIDDEN / REALM_SCOPE_MISMATCH — cached token valid but minted for a different identity,
  e.g. after a signed-in-user switch; a 403-triggered refresh also forces the live WebSocket to
  reconnect). OnAuthError fires when a 401/403 survives the refresh — tear down and rebuild.
- An Arca instance is bound to the identity its tokens are minted for: on identity change call
  Dispose() and build a fresh instance with the new user's provider.

## Initialization

```go
// API key (backend)
client, _ := arca.New(arca.Config{APIKey: "arca_...", Realm: "my-realm"})
// Scoped token (realm read from claims)
client, _ := arca.FromToken(jwt, arca.Config{})
// Auto-refreshing token
client, _ := arca.FromTokenProvider(provider, arca.Config{Realm: "my-realm"})

client.Ready(ctx) // resolve realm slug -> id (also lazy on first call)
```

## Operation handles

Mutations return *arca.OperationHandle[T] (HTTP runs in background):
- h.Submitted(ctx) (T, error)  — HTTP response before settlement
- h.Wait(ctx) (T, error)       — blocks until terminal state
- h.WaitTimeout(ctx, d)        — explicit settlement timeout
- h.Predicted                  — *PredictedEffect (sync, optimistic)

PlaceOrder/ClosePosition return *arca.OrderHandle (embeds OperationHandle):
- order.Filled(ctx) (SimOrderWithFills, error)
- order.OnFill(ctx, func(SimFill)) func()
- order.FillSummary(ctx) (*Fill, error)
- order.Cancel(ctx, path) (*OperationHandle[OrderOperationResponse], error)
- order.Resize(ctx, newSize, path) (*OperationHandle[OrderOperationResponse], error) // sized orders only; unsized triggers rejected

StreamCashV9WalletAccount is the single connection (returns *CashV9WalletAccountStreamDisconnectedError with LastRevision) |

Kinds set_up_account, send, enable_automatic_deposits (route + permit), revoke_automatic_deposits, source_send; accepted answers execute without the client |
| One owner-facing wallet, rendered as-is | client.GetCashV9WalletAccount(ctx, boundaryID) / GetCashV9WalletAccountByOwner(ctx, ownerAddress) → CashV9WalletAccount — WalletState (setup_required · setting_up · ready · needs_attention · unavailable) + Attention reasons, Balances{ConfirmedMicro, AvailableMicro, ReservedMicro, PendingInMicro, PendingOutMicro, AsOf}, Source (linked external address: BalanceMicro nil when unknown, Health, its own AsOf), Operations[] (kind create_cash/send/deposit/receiver; state sending/confirming/completed/failed; Reason only when failed; CanRetry), Revision. Durable records only, no chain call; *NotFoundError for an unknown boundary/owner; arca:ReadObject is enough (a realm-scoped device token works) |

## Venue-to-venue hops

A transfer whose From AND To are both exchange objects is a **venue hop**: value goes venue-to-venue in one on-chain frame and never rests at a boundary, so no intermediate denominated arca is needed. Plain `Transfer` performs it. Hops carry **no fee** (a non-zero one is refused, not ignored) and work across isolation boundaries. Destinations are limited to Hyperliquid and the paper venue; a GLL-paper target is refused because its account is faucet-credited rather than credited by value landing at the venue contract.

`HopVenues` is `Transfer` **plus the co-sign fallback**, and is what to reach for when the source boundary might be armed. On an unarmed boundary it is exactly a transfer and `Sign` is never invoked; on an armed one the plain call is refused (the kernel will not move value out unsigned) so it proposes, calls `Sign(ctx, digest, proposal)`, and submits. `Sign` is a `CosignDigestSigner` — an HSM, a KMS, a hardware wallet; the SDK never holds this key. Leave it nil and an armed boundary returns `*CosignRequiredError`, whose `Challenge` names `Surface` / `BoundaryID` / `Propose` / `Submit`. Unlike `*StepUpRequiredError` there is no handler hook and no auto-retry: a browser confirmation is something the platform can drive, a co-signature is not.

`ProposeVenueHop` / `SubmitVenueHop` expose the halves when you want to drive it yourself. `Path` is required at propose and must match at submit — the signed `Ref` derives from it.

**`HopVenues` verifies the proposal before it calls `Sign`, and so should you if you drive the halves yourself.** A digest is 32 opaque bytes: a key asked to sign one cannot tell a hop to your own paper account from a hop to a stranger's, and neither can a user staring at a device prompt. `proposal.Verify()` re-derives the `paramsHash` and the EIP-712 digest from the proposal's own readable fields and returns an error unless both match what the server sent — so a propose response that quietly changed the destination sub-account or raised the amount is refused locally rather than discovered on chain. It also pins the EIP-712 domain to this SDK's own `ArcaCustodyKernel` / version `"2"` constants rather than trusting the response, so a signature cannot be moved onto a kernel whose semantics this SDK has never seen.

The pieces are exported for callers who want them directly: `TransferBetweenVenuesParamsHash`, `OperatorActionDigest`, `CosignDomainSeparator`, and — for a backend that holds the key rather than delegating to an HSM — `SignCosignDigest(privKey, digest)` and `SignVenueHop(privKey, proposal)` (which verifies first, then signs). Encode `AmountRaw`, never the decimal `Amount`. All of it is pinned byte-for-byte against the Solidity implementation by the shared cross-SDK golden vectors.

**Co-sign nonce lifecycle.** Submitting an envelope whose nonce is already spent returns `*CosignNonceUsedError` (412 `COSIGN_NONCE_USED`), carrying `Details.BoundaryID` / `Nonce` / `Resolution` / `Reason` (`nonce_consumed` on a marker 7+ burn-set kernel, `counter_stale` on a marker 3-6 counter kernel; both resolve identically, so one branch works across generations). **This is not a signature failure** — the signature was very likely fine, the slot it committed to is gone (a retry raced the original, or the user cancelled). Give it its own branch that re-proposes and re-signs. Treat it as blocked-pending-user, never retryable: replaying the same envelope can never succeed, so a reconciler must re-propose. `client.GetCosignNonceState(ctx, boundaryID, nonce)` checks the slot BEFORE submitting (a proxy of the kernel's `isCosignNonceConsumed` view, so no chain client is needed) — read `Spendable`, not `Consumed`: a counter kernel has no burn set and reports `Consumed=false` even for nonces it will refuse, carrying `CounterNonce` instead. Nonces are minted in `[1, 2^63-1]` and carried as decimal strings (the 63-bit rather than 64-bit ceiling keeps every value inside a positive signed int64).

**`Disposition` is the field a reconciler branches on, not `Reason`.** Both `*CosignNonceUsedError`'s `Details` and `GetCosignNonceState` carry `Disposition` (`arca.CosignNonceExecuted` | `CosignNonceRevoked` | `CosignNonceUnknown`), `TxHash`, and — for an execution the platform submitted — `OperationID`. `Reason` names which nonce lane refused; `Disposition` names the CAUSE, and the two causes are opposite facts about whether the customer's money moved: executed means the action already ran (reconcile against `OperationID`; do NOT re-send), revoked means the owner cancelled the slot with `invalidateCosignNonce` and nothing moved (safe to fail or re-propose; there is no `OperationID`, since the owner acted directly on the kernel). Unknown means the attributing log fell outside the platform's lookback window or the chain read failed — it is **not** evidence that nothing happened, and only revoked licenses asserting that. Empty when `Spendable` is true (nothing burned it, so there is nothing to attribute) and empty from an older server, which stays distinguishable from unknown. The SDK narrows any unrecognized value to `CosignNonceUnknown`, so a future disposition can never reach a `default` arm written as "not executed, so nothing moved".

**The EIP-712 domain version is `"2"` on kernel marker 7, and that is breaking for a client that re-derives digests.** The struct is unchanged, so relaying the server's digest is unaffected; rebuilding it against a pinned `"1"` refuses every co-signed action and reports it as a mismatch rather than a version error. `proposal.Verify()` pins the version this SDK was built against on purpose (a signature must not be movable onto a kernel whose semantics this SDK has never seen), which makes a realm's kernel upgrade and an SDK upgrade one step. If you derive digests yourself, read `proposal.Domain.Version`.

## Watch streams (real-time)

All return a stream with OnUpdate(cb) func(), Updates() <-chan T, Ready(ctx),
State(), OnStateChange, Close().

| Method | Stream value |
|---|---|
| client.WatchPrices(ctx, *WatchPricesOptions) | map[string]string (+ Get/Prices) |
| client.WatchOperations(ctx, path) | Operation |
| client.WatchBalances(ctx, path) | BalanceUpdate |
| client.WatchObject(ctx, path) | ObjectValuation |
| client.WatchObjects(ctx, paths) | map[string]ObjectValuation |
| client.WatchAggregation(ctx, sources) | PathAggregation |
| client.WatchExchangeState(ctx, id) | ExchangeState |
| client.WatchFills(ctx, id, opts) | Fill |
| client.WatchRealmFills(ctx, *WatchRealmFillsOptions{FromCursor}) | RealmFillUpdate{Fill, Cursor, Replayed} |
| client.WatchRealmExchange(ctx) | RealmExchangeUpdate{ObjectID, ObjectPath, State, Resync} |
| client.WatchFunding(ctx, id) | FundingPayment |
| client.WatchCandles(ctx, coins, intervals) | CandleUpdate |
| client.WatchOI(ctx, coins, intervals) | OIUpdate |
| client.WatchTrades(ctx, coins) | MarketTrade |
| client.WatchTwap(ctx, exchangeId, opId) | Twap |

WatchRealmFills is the realm-wide at-least-once fill stream: catch-up from
the durable log (ListRealmFills asc) from FromCursor, then live fill.recorded
tail; replays from its cursor on gap/reconnect/resync. It subscribes by event
TYPE (subscribe_events), not by watching "/" — a realm-root path watch makes
the server assemble a full-realm snapshot and hold a realm-wide valuation
watch this stream discards. Contract: persist
u.Cursor after processing, pass back as FromCursor on restart; process
idempotently keyed on Fill.ID (duplicates possible, loss never). Empty
FromCursor starts from now (no history). Delivery starts on first
OnUpdate/Updates/Ready attach.

WatchRealmExchange is the realm-wide live-tail of exchange.updated — the
no-fill mutations (funding, deposit/withdraw, isolated margin, leverage,
margin-mode) that fill.recorded does not cover. Same wire as
WatchRealmFills (subscribe_events, not a path watch of "/"). There is no
durable log: a gap or reconnect emits Resync=true and the consumer
re-seeds the books it already holds. Live events carry the serve-path
open book (State.Positions include liquidationPrice). This stream never
fans out GetExchangeState. Delivery starts on first OnUpdate/Updates/Ready
attach. Not mid-driven — exchange.mid_price is a different type.

Knowing when an exchange arca can trade: creating one returns before its venue
account exists, and until it does every trading call answers 503
EXCHANGE_PROVISIONING. Two events replace polling for it.
EventExchangeProvisioned ("exchange.provisioned") means the venue account exists
and its metadata is stamped, so the object stops answering 503.
EventExchangeReady ("exchange.ready") means the trading agent is registered on
chain and it can actually trade. Both carry RealmEvent.Exchange
(*ExchangeProvisioning: ObjectID, Path, CosignRequired, Tradable,
AccountAddress, AgentWalletID).

They are separate because on a cosign-armed boundary they are separate moments:
the account is provisioned, but its trading agent needs the user to co-sign a
grant, so provisioned arrives with CosignRequired=true and ready follows only
once that grant lands — minutes or days later. Treat the gap as waiting on the
user, not a stall. On an unarmed boundary both arrive together.

EventDepositDetected ("deposit.detected") is money seen arriving at a watched
deposit address before it has been swept and become balance;
RealmEvent.Deposit (*DetectedDeposit) carries it. Chain truth, not ledger truth
— EventBalanceUpdated is still what says the funds landed.

Aggregation sources: arca.NewPrefixSource(p), NewPathsSource(paths),
NewPatternSource(p), NewWatchSource(id).

Lower-level access: client.WS() returns *WebSocketManager (On(type, cb),
typed OnX listeners, OnGap, OnAuthenticated, OnRotated, EnsureConnected,
RotateConnection, Disconnect).

OnGap(func(missed int64)) fires on delivery loss, from either source: a hole
the client observed in the server-assigned deliverySeq (missed is exact), or
a server-sent stream.resync marker announcing that events were dropped before
they were sequenced — a loss no sequence check can see (missed is a floor of
1). Both mean the same thing: refetch. Watch streams already do this
internally; register OnGap only for state you track yourself.

Gapless rotation: the connection is proactively replaced before the
infrastructure's maximum socket lifetime severs it. A replacement is warmed
alongside the live one — authenticated, fully re-subscribed, confirmed by the
server — and only then takes over, so delivery never pauses. Automatic; nothing
to call. Config.ConnectionLifetime overrides the default (50m), and a lifetime
reported by the server wins over it. A pointer to 0 disables rotation and
outranks both, including a server-reported cap, so the opt-out still works on
the production fleet — at the cost of an unplanned reconnect. No status
change is emitted across a rotation and there is no delivery gap; OnRotated
fires for per-connection server state that the swap cannot carry over (watch
streams handle their own). WS().RotateConnection() forces one, returning false
when there is no healthy connection or a handoff is already under way.

## Address observations

Read-only watching of EXTERNAL wallets for ERC-20 Transfer logs on one configured
chain/token (HyperEVM 999 / USDC first), delivered as durable, replayable events
with a contiguous per-realm Sequence (a gap is lost delivery, never a legitimate
hole). Disabled by default on every deployment; a realm must be admitted by the
operator (403 OBSERVATION_REALM_NOT_ADMITTED / 503 OBSERVATION_DISABLED until then).
An observation is a fact about a public chain — never a ledger credit or a spending
authorisation; coalesce arrivals into your own authorised follow-up job.
Amounts, chain ids, block numbers, sequences and revisions are decimal STRINGS in
raw token units ("1000000" = 1 USDC): parse with math/big, never float64.
Effect.FundingDelta is the receipt amount (positive incoming; "0" for outgoing,
self, zero-value and transfer.removed); DeltaRaw is signed bookkeeping — never
trigger forwarding from it. Persist batch.Cursor in the SAME transaction as your
inbox and dedupe by EventID (stable; redelivery is normal). Typed errors:
*ObservationCursorExpiredError (take a snapshot, rebuild, record the gap — never
invent receipts from a balance difference), *ObservationStreamResetError
(reset_required control frame), *ObservationStreamDisconnectedError{LastCursor}
(EOF; RunAddressObservationStream retries it), *ObservationSchemaError (unknown
schemaVersion — upgrade, do not guess). Contract: documents/contracts/address-observations.md.

## V9 cash Wallet Account (one read per wallet)

GetCashV9WalletAccount composes what a wallet screen needs from Arca's durable
records — the V9 cash boundary plus the address watch on its owner — so a product
renders it instead of re-deriving it from the account read, the observer and chain
calls. Money is micro-USDC integer STRINGS (parse with math/big). Every figure
carries an AsOf {Block, Hash, Time}: Balances.AsOf is the realm's confirmed
observation cursor, Source.AsOf the observer's complete-through checkpoint; they
may differ — show the older one, never block on equality. Freshness is not a state:
WalletState says whether the account is usable (unavailable = the durable
projection disagrees with the journal; balances are still returned as last-known),
not whether the data is recent. Operations lists every non-terminal operation plus
30 days of terminal ones (≤200, newest first); ReservedMicro == PendingOutMicro by
design (ledger hold vs the owner's "money leaving"). awaiting_approval (unsigned
intent) and uncertain (lost reply) are states the PRODUCT layer adds from its own
records; Arca has no operation before a signature is accepted. AutoDeposit is nil
until Arca observes adapter routes. Fixtures for every state:
backend/libs/arca-go/cashv9/testdata/wallet-account/. Contract:
documents/contracts/v9-cash-wallet-integration.md ("Wallet Account read model").

Stream instead of poll: RunCashV9WalletAccountStream(ctx, boundaryID, accept)
delivers a COMPLETE CashV9WalletAccount on connect and after every change to the
boundary (change journal) or to the linked address (observation feed), at most
one per 250 ms; heartbeats every 20 s. Every frame is the whole state, so a
missed frame costs latency, never correctness — treat each callback as "replace
what you show". Resume is automatic: the last snapshot's Revision is sent as
Last-Event-ID and the server answers with one fresh snapshot (the ingress resets
connections about hourly; Run reconnects with 1 s→30 s backoff and resets it
after a delivered snapshot). It returns only on ctx cancellation, a callback
error, or a refused connection: *NotFoundError (unknown boundary),
*ForbiddenError, or a 429 (code V9_WALLET_ACCOUNT_STREAMS_EXCEEDED) when one key
holds more than the per-replica cap (16 by default) — shard keys per product
backend rather than retrying. Do not hold a stream AND poll GetCashV9WalletAccount.

Requirements lists the action-proposal attempts awaiting the owner's answer
(CashV9WalletRequirement: ProposalID, RequirementID, AttemptID, ActionKind,
SchemaID, Variant, ExpiresAt unix seconds), soonest deadline first. An answered,
expired or admitted attempt is not listed; read the proposal for its payload.

## Wallet action proposals (request one action, answer its requirements)

A product requests ONE action for a wallet owner; Arca answers with the exact
signatures it needs or the typed reasons it cannot. Supported kinds:
set_up_account (CashPath + SourceAddress = owner), send (CashObjectID,
AmountMicro, exactly one of Destination / DestinationCashObjectID), and the
relay-executed enable_automatic_deposits, revoke_automatic_deposits and
source_send (PrivyObjectID + SourceWalletID = a verified provider wallet at the
Cash owner's address, CashObjectID; source_send adds AmountMicro + Destination;
route actions may name DepositLinkID). An activation returns TWO requirements,
req_route and req_permit, answered separately; its operation exists only once
both are stored. A realm with no execution relay answers the relay-executed
kinds with limitation unsupported_action.

```go
p, err := client.ProposeWalletAction(ctx, arca.WalletActionRequest{
    RequestID: "send-7f3c", // your idempotency key: same request → same proposal
    RequestedAction: arca.WalletRequestedAction{Kind: "send", CashObjectID: cashObjectID,
        AmountMicro: "500000", Destination: "0x…"},
})
for _, r := range p.Requirements { // r.State "awaiting_approval": sign r.TypedDataJSON
    // verify r.TypedDataJSON / r.Scope against your own policy, then have the owner sign
    p, err = client.RespondWalletRequirement(ctx, p.ProposalID, r.ID, arca.WalletRequirementResponse{
        AttemptID: r.AttemptID, PayloadHash: r.PayloadHash, Decision: "approve",
        Signature: sig, IdempotencyKey: "approve-" + r.AttemptID})
}
// p.Limitations: account_not_set_up · deposit_permission_missing · deposit_permission_unknown ·
// resource_conflict · unsupported_action · unsupported_schema_version · policy_capability_missing
```

Rules: a read (GetWalletActionProposal, the Wallet Account) never issues work. An
attempt that expired unsigned is replaced only when you POST the identical request
again (the old attempt reads expired with SupersededBy). Decline
(Decision "decline", no signature) is durable. Answering anything but the open
attempt returns ACTION_ATTEMPT_STALE (*ConflictError, Details["limitation"]
"attempt_stale"); a signature after its deadline returns V9_CONSENT_EXPIRED. A
lost reply: resend the SAME response — it returns the same operation. Once
accepted, Arca executes without the client; follow Operations[] or the Wallet
Account stream. Missing and unknown deposit permission are different facts —
never render unknown as revoked. Contract: documents/contracts/v9-wallet-intents.md.

## Admin (realm-less builder client)

```go
admin := arca.NewAdmin(arca.AdminConfig{Token: builderJWT})
admin.SignInWithGoogle / GetMe / Refresh / Logout
admin.MintToken / MintDeviceToken
admin.CreateRealm / ListRealms / GetRealm / DeleteRealm / UpdateRealmSettings
admin.CreateApiKey / ListApiKeys / RevokeApiKey
admin.ListMyOrgs / CreateOrg / GetOrg / GetActiveTerms / AcceptTerms
admin.ListMembers / UpdateMember / RemoveMember / InviteMember / ListInvitations
admin.GetCredentialScope / ListAuthAuditLog / TransferOwnership
```

## Step-up auth (412)

Set arca.Config.StepUpHandler (or admin SetStepUpHandler):
func(ctx, arca.StepUpChallenge) (string, error) — return a single-use step-up
JWT. The SDK retries once and never persists it. Returning an error surfaces
*StepUpCancelledError.

## Anti-patterns

1. Reuse a nonce path on retry; do not call Nonce inside a retry loop.
2. Always Ready(ctx) (or call any method, which is lazy) before relying on realm id.
3. Use canonical coin ids ("hl:0:BTC", never "BTC").
4. FundAccount/DefundAccount are dev-only; use CreatePaymentLink in production.
5. size is base-asset units, not USD. Min notional is $10 (GetOrderLimits()).
6. Isolated-only markets (MarginModes == ["isolated"], i.e. deprecated OnlyIsolated) require Isolated:true + positive Leverage when opening/increasing on PlaceOrder; a ReduceOnly close/trim is accepted without Leverage (uses the position's current leverage, never re-margins). Independent of HIP-3 — some HIP-3 markets (e.g. hl:1:TSLA) are cross-eligible.

## Chart history is already marked; `points` is a ceiling

GetEquityHistory and GetPnlHistory are ONE computation — same buckets, same
marking; P&L history is equity history minus external flows. Every bucket's
EquityUsd is that bucket's cash valued at that bucket's own mids PLUS
unrealized P&L on every position open at that bucket, valued at the same mids.
It is not settled equity carried forward and the marking is not limited to the
live point, so do NOT rebuild the curve from candles: a rebuild that projects
the CURRENT position backwards has no term for a closed position, a realized
loss, or a liquidation, and silently flat-lines the days before the newest
position. Status describes the CASH side's provenance, not whether the point
was marked — ChartCarried means no ledger event landed in that bucket, and such
a point still changes value as the market moves. ChartIncomplete is the
degradation signal (a mid was missing, or the position overlay could not run).
Deposits move EquityUsd and never move PnlUsd, so chart EquityUsd (present on
PnlPoint too) for "what is this account worth".

EquityUsd is FLOORED at zero and the floor never destroys the number. Exchange
accounts are the one class permitted to hold a negative balance, and a negative
balance is worse to render than a zero. When the floor clamps a point the true
signed value comes back as UnflooredEquityUsd; when it does not, that field is
empty — so its presence is also the only way to tell a floored point from a
genuinely-zero one. PnlUsd is derived from the UNFLOORED value: a signed
performance delta must not be flattened by a balance clamp.

`points` is a CEILING: the ladder picks the finest rung whose bucket count fits
inside it, so a 24h window at points=180 is served at 15m (~96 points). The
response describes its own grid via Resolution + BucketSeconds, with
ResolutionRequested set only when coverage forced a promotion. Reconcile two
sources for the same series by window and resolution — never by "whichever has
more points", which a client-side reconstruction wins every time regardless of
correctness. PickResolution/BucketMs/AlignDown make the count predictable
before the request.

## Folder labels: PatchFolderLabels merges, UpdateFolderLabels overwrites

Folders are virtual aggregations of arca paths, so folder labels live in their own store keyed by (realmId, path) and are surfaced inline on BrowseObjects rows. Three operations: GetFolderLabels reads the current set (empty map when none are set); UpdateFolderLabels REPLACES the whole set (an empty map deletes every label); PatchFolderLabels MERGES a per-key delta (nil pointer removes a key, unmentioned keys keep their value, an empty map is a no-op, removing the last key deletes the row). Prefer PatchFolderLabels whenever you mean to change some keys rather than define all of them — e.g. flipping a projection privacy label on a user folder. The server merges inside one transaction, so two concurrent single-key writes both land; a read-then-UpdateFolderLabels round trip loses whichever write commits first. Validation (32 keys, key grammar `^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9._-]*$`, `arca.`/`_` reserved prefixes, 256-char values) runs on the MERGED result, so a one-key patch can still be rejected for pushing the folder past the ceiling.

## TP/SL is an OCO bracket; cancelled orders carry a reason

SetPositionTpsl stamps one auto-generated OcoGroupID on both legs; when either fills (even partially) the venue cancels the other and sets CancelReason="sibling_filled". Pass an explicit OcoGroupID (on SetPositionTpslOptions, SetPositionTriggerOptions, or PlaceOrderOptions) to build or reuse your own bracket — it is advisory metadata, forwarded to the venue but NOT part of the order signature. A CANCELLED SimOrder exposes CancelReason (one of user_requested, sibling_filled, position_closed, position_flipped, liquidated, position_gone, market_delisted, insufficient_margin), readable on-demand via GetOrder / ListOrders. insufficient_margin is the one to handle in code: placement checks margin but does not RESERVE it, so a resting limit order can become unaffordable while it waits, and the venue retires it after it has repeatedly reached its price unaffordably over several minutes. Treat it as "free up margin, then re-place", not as a transient error to retry blindly. Two placement rules match Hyperliquid: an ALO (post-only) limit that would immediately cross the book is rejected (use GTC/IOC to take liquidity), and a trigger set on the wrong side of the current mark (one that would fire immediately) is rejected.

Sized (partial) TP/SL: a TP/SL leg closes the WHOLE position by default (SizeToMax). To scale out a fixed quantity instead, set a base-unit size — Size on SetPositionTriggerOptions (SetStopLoss/SetTakeProfit), or StopLossSz/TakeProfitSz on SetPositionTpslOptions. A sized leg is a reduce-only partial (capped at the live position size). It is NOT exempt from the $10 minimum — only an exact close is — so size scale-out legs to clear the floor. Because a partial fill of one OCO leg cancels its sibling, SetPositionTpsl does NOT auto-link the two legs when either is sized — so a TP that scales out half does not cancel the stop guarding the remainder. Pass an explicit OcoGroupID if you deliberately want sized legs linked.

## OpenWithBracket opens a position + TP/SL as one linked normalTpsl bracket

OpenWithBracket(ctx, OpenBracketOptions{Path, ObjectID, Market, Side, Size, TakeProfitPx?, StopLossPx?, TakeProfitSz?, StopLossSz?, ...}) opens a position and attaches its reduce-only TP/SL triggers as a linked normalTpsl bracket (Hyperliquid parity). The entry and its trigger legs are submitted as a single signed batch to one operation (POST /objects/{id}/exchange/orders/batch): one signature links the legs. This is NOT globally all-or-none — Hyperliquid only guarantees whole-payload rejection for pre-validation failures. The trigger legs ARM ONLY WHEN THE ENTRY FILLS — they can't fire on mark price before the position exists — and the venue server-stamps a shared OCO group on them (the entry is excluded). Returns OpenBracketResult with one *OrderHandle per leg (Entry, TakeProfit, StopLoss), all backed by the single bracket operation; each handle's Filled/OnFill/Cancel targets that leg. Until the entry fills, a TP/SL child is NOT yet a live venue order (no venue order id — addressable only by its cloid); its handle matches fills by cloid, and cancelling it before activation cancels the parent bracket. At least one of TakeProfitPx/StopLossPx is required. normalTpsl is a FIXED-SIZE parent-order bracket: each trigger child defaults to the ENTRY's Size (a fixed-size leg of the parent order, NOT a whole-position SizeToMax trigger); set TakeProfitSz / StopLossSz for a smaller partial-close child. For a WHOLE-POSITION TP/SL that sizes to the entire live position (Hyperliquid positionTpsl), use SetStopLoss / SetTakeProfit / SetPositionTpsl instead — a separate trigger-only model with no entry leg that is not accepted here. Caveat: the bracket's legs share one server-stamped OCO group, so a partial TP fill cancels the SL on the remainder; to "scale out half and keep a stop on the rest", open the bracket with only the sized TP and attach the SL separately via SetStopLoss.

## Resize / ModifyOrder on Hyperliquid is a cancel-replace

order.Resize(ctx, newSize, path) / client.ModifyOrder(...) treats newSize as the new TOTAL order size. On Hyperliquid this is a cancel-replace: the venue cancels the old order id and places a replacement with a NEW order id, retaining the cloid. The platform re-correlates later fills/cancels on the replacement back to the original placement operation automatically. newSize must exceed the already-filled quantity (a resize at-or-below the filled amount is rejected). Unsized (SizeToMax) whole-position triggers have no size to amend and are rejected.

## Not yet ported (REST equivalents available)

Merged chart streams (WatchEquityChart/WatchPnlChart/WatchCandleChart) and the
derived WatchMaxOrderSize are not in this release. Use GetEquityHistory,
GetPnlHistory, GetCandles plus the arca ladder helpers (PickResolution,
BucketMs, ComputeChartRange) and WatchAggregation to build equivalent behavior.

Account contract: use OrderHandle.Confirmed(ctx) for immediate execution or
intentional resting placement, Submitted for HTTP acknowledgement, Wait for
operation settlement. Never resubmit an uncertain mutation. GetOperationOrder
reads the original account/order; ReconcileOrderKey can only certify absence
through a durable supported fence. GetExchangeCapabilities replaces builder
venue conditionals. Mutations do not retry network/502/503/504; ArcaError retains
StatusCode and Details. Projection endpoints, PatchObjectLabels and scalar/pair
ActiveAssetData.AvailableToTradeRaw are supported. Decimal money must remain
exact; missing evidence is unknown, not zero.


### Terminal execution receipts

`OrderHandle.ExecutionReceipt(ctx)` returns terminal execution evidence immediately
when the HTTP operation already contains it; it does not wait for a WebSocket ACK,
order-history reads, or individual ledger fills. Nonterminal responses use scoped
execution updates and an acknowledged snapshot. `Confirmed` keeps its existing
response type and uses this receipt path for immediate orders.

The receipt includes original `RequestedSize`, executed `FilledSize`, known
`RemainingSize`, `FulfillmentState`, and `RemainingDisposition`. Unknown original
intent stays unknown. A terminal IOC may be only partially fulfilled. Venue
aggregate prices have `AveragePriceFinal=false`; do not present them as exact
final VWAP. `FillsComplete=false` is independent of terminal execution.

`GetOperationExecutionReceipt(ctx, objectID, operation)` recovers from the original
operation before requesting account-scoped history. It rejects a different account
and never submits a replacement. `Filled` retains its full-order return type and
performs a metadata read after execution; unavailable or stale details remain an
error. Use `ExecutionReceipt` for prompt confirmation.

### Execution vs. accounting: `Accounted`

The receipt proves terminal execution at the venue. The ledger commit that updates
the account's positions and balances happens afterwards, and a
`GetExchangeState` / `WatchExchangeState` read taken in between returns the
pre-accounting snapshot. `OrderHandle.Accounted(ctx)` returns once every executed
quantity is recorded (the platform's `FillsComplete`), so an account read taken
after it includes the execution; refresh account state on it, not on the receipt.
Push-first — each `fill.recorded` for the order, a delivery gap, or a reconnect
triggers one order read — with a bounded backoff read (500 ms doubling to 8 s)
for a lost push, until ctx expires (pass a deadline-bound ctx; it returns
`ctx.Err()`). On venues whose order read carries no `FillsComplete`, completion is
the recorded fills for the order covering its executed size exactly (`big.Rat`,
never float). A zero-fill terminal order returns at once; a failed placement
returns the failure. When it returns, any live `WatchExchangeState` for the account
is refreshed.

### The observation says what it does not include yet: `AccountingPending`

On the platform mirror every `ExchangeState` (REST and stream) carries
`AccountingPending []AccountingPendingExecution`: one entry per venue-confirmed
execution the ledger has not fully recorded, with `OperationID`, `OrderID`,
`Market`, `Side`, `ExecutedSize`, `AccountedSize`, `UnaccountedSize` (executed
minus accounted — the only quantity to add on top of `Positions`),
`ExecutionFinal` and a provisional `AveragePrice`. The frame emitted at execution
time lists the whole execution, each per-fill frame lists what is still missing,
the settled frame lists nothing, so `Positions + AccountingPending` is the same
book on every frame and no reader has to guess whether a frame is "after" an
execution — whoever placed the order. `state.ProjectedPositions()` composes it
(reductions keep their entry, increases blend by quantity, opens/reversals take
the execution price, flat markets vanish, a malformed entry falls back to the
ledger row); `state.AccountingSettled()` is `len(AccountingPending) == 0`.
Render the projection; apply a frame's money only when settled — realized P&L
and fees are ledger facts and are never projected. Absent on venues whose
accounting is synchronous with execution. `Accounted` remains the per-order
wait; this is the per-observation description that makes the wait unnecessary
for display.

### Attaching to an order placed elsewhere

`OrderHandleFor(ctx, objectID, operationID)` returns an `*OrderHandle` for an order
this client did not place. Every other order factory is a mutation, so a caller
holding only an operation id had no supported way to obtain a handle; calling
`PlaceOrder` again would be a second submission, not a read. This performs one
`GetOperation` read and binds the handle to that order, so `Accounted`,
`ExecutionReceipt`, `Filled`, `Fills` and `OnFill` work on it exactly as on a placed
order. It places, cancels and resizes nothing; `Cancel` / `Resize` remain explicit
opt-in mutations. An operation that is not an order, or whose recorded input names a
different `exchangeObjectId`, returns `ORDER_IDENTITY_MISMATCH` — an id from another
account never resolves into a handle on this one; absent input is not a mismatch.
`Confirmed`'s immediate/resting classification is reconstructed from the operation's
recorded intent. As with `PlaceOrder`, ctx governs the handle's event capture.

`WatchExchangeState` re-reads on a `deliverySeq` gap or `stream.resync` marker, on
reconnect, and — on a 1 s→30 s backoff — while an observation is invalidated
(`exchangeStateUnavailable` / expired `validUntil`); every re-read is guarded by the
observation epoch so an older read never overwrites a newer push.
`stream.Refresh()` re-reads on demand (non-blocking, coalesced).
## General operation recovery

Operation waits register listeners before subscribing. Startup, actual gaps, reauthentication and sparse operation notifications recover behind a fresh correlated ACK, with at most three failed attempts. Healthy pending operations do not poll. Terminal pushes win during recovery; cancellation releases only the owned watch. No timeout automatically replays a mutation.

Operation snapshot evidence: Terminal operations in the initial or buffered subscription snapshot resolve the wait before any HTTP read, including typed failed/expired results. Socket rotation requests fresh operation evidence on the replacement connection; its pong only establishes transport readiness. Stale snapshot request IDs and unrelated operation IDs cannot settle the wait.
Verified snapshot operations are shared with all live waiters, including results buffered while another caller refreshes the same root watch; each waiter still accepts only its original operation ID.
